title: Jailer 2 Opens Near ₹125 Crore Worldwide as Rajinikanth Tops His Own Record
excerpt: Sacnilk puts day one at ₹125.25 crore worldwide — ₹70.25 crore gross in India and ₹55 crore overseas — with the Hindi version posting the third-biggest dubbed Kollywood opening ever.
body:
• Jailer 2 collected ₹125.25 crore worldwide on day one (Sacnilk): ₹70.25 crore gross in India and ₹55 crore overseas.
  • India net was ₹59.70 crore across 16,599 shows — Tamil ₹43.35 crore, Telugu ₹12.50 crore, Hindi ₹3.50 crore, Kannada ₹0.35 crore.
  • The Hindi version's ₹3.50 crore net makes it the third-biggest Hindi-dubbed Kollywood opening ever, behind Rajinikanth's own 2.0 (₹20.25 crore) and Kabali (₹5.21 crore), per Koimoi.
  • Chennai occupancy hit 90.8% overall and 97% for night shows; the first Jailer ended its run above ₹604.50 crore worldwide.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has opened to ₹125.25 crore worldwide on its first day, according to Sacnilk's day-one tally, as the sequel outgrossed most trade expectations and delivered the superstar a career-best opening stretch across formats. India contributed ₹70.25 crore gross (₹59.70 crore net across 16,599 shows) and overseas markets ₹55 crore, Koimoi and Sacnilk reported.

The opening builds on ₹38 crore in advance bookings, and fans from Chennai to Japan and Dubai turned release day into a festival of first-day-first-show celebrations. Day-one footfalls in India alone were 3.75 million, Sacnilk said. All figures are early tracker estimates, not producer numbers.

Where the Money Came From

Tamil led the India net with ₹43.35 crore, followed by Telugu at ₹12.50 crore, Hindi at ₹3.50 crore and Kannada at ₹0.35 crore. State-wise grosses: Tamil Nadu ₹24 crore, Andhra Pradesh–Telangana ₹14.50 crore, Karnataka ₹14.50 crore, Kerala ₹12.50 crore and the rest of India ₹4.75 crore.

Occupancy in the Tamil version was strongest in the home market: Chennai 90.8% overall with night shows at 97%, Coimbatore 91.3%, Pondicherry 90.3%, Kochi 82.5% and Trichy 84.8%. Bengaluru ran at 69.8% and Hyderabad's Telugu shows at 65%. The Hindi version was softer in the north — Mumbai 25%, the National Capital Region 27.3%, Pune 33% — the usual pattern for a dubbed southern release on day one.

A Record Against Himself

Koimoi's ranking of Hindi-dubbed Kollywood openings puts Jailer 2's Hindi version third of all time at ₹3.40–3.80 crore net — behind only Rajinikanth's own 2.0 (₹20.25 crore) and Kabali (₹5.21 crore), and ahead of Kanguva (₹3.25 crore) and Leo (₹2.85 crore). The debut also made Jailer 2, in a single day, the fifth-highest-grossing Tamil film of 2026 worldwide, Koimoi noted, and the sixth Tamil film of the year to cross ₹100 crore.

The Bar Set by the First Film

The original Jailer finished above ₹604.50 crore worldwide in 2023. Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Sun Pictures, the sequel returns Rajinikanth as Muthuvel Pandian with Ramya Krishnan and Yogi Babu, adds SJ Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty and Vidya Balan, and stacks cameos from Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar, Jackie Shroff and Vijay Sethupathi, with music by Anirudh Ravichander.

What's Next

Trade watchers will judge the film on the weekend hold: an opening built on fan shows needs family audiences on days two and three. On day-one evidence — near-full houses in Tamil Nadu and a record dubbed debut — Jailer 2 has started exactly where a sequel of this scale needed to.
